newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN CRUDE - LIGHT GRADES SEE ACTIVE TRADING.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN CRUDE - LIGHT GRADES SEE ACTIVE TRADING.

text.p: Asia's heavy crude market was steady
Middle East crude market was fundamentally balanced, with the last September barrels of Abu Dhabi grades expected to be committed soon.
"They'll probably get sold by today. If not they'll be rolled over to October" said a trader with a major oil company.
"But it's not a big volume, anyway" he added.
Discussion on price levels were not heard, although selling interest had been heard at ADNOC +0.10 for Murban and ADNOC +0.15 for Lower Zakum.
Despite Masila cargoes still on offer, tby two western traders and a Japanese trading house.
But this was not weighing down the market, since there was buying interest heard, from China and from a US major.
Asia's light crudes traded at higher levels, as refiners actively look to cover their September requirements, traders said on Thursday.
September Belida was sold by a shosha to a European major at ICP +40 cents per barrel.
This is higher than a Belida trade done by another shosha earlier this week at ICP +30.
September trading for Indonesian crudes normally start only when the monthly allocations are announced in the middle of August.
But limited availabilities of other light crudes have prompted buyers to emerge earlier this time, to prevent being caught short.
Prices of Belida Belida have risen compared to the early August deals done below ICP +20.
The firmness in Belida prices led Malaysia to move up its offer price of September Tapis, to APPI +20/25 cents from an earlier offer of APPI +15.
Trading on Australian crudes was thin, although a producer confirmed selling another September Cossack at Tapis APPI -57 cents.
The seller had acquired this cargo from a shosha last week at Tapis APPI -80.
The last Cossack trade was by the same seller to China at Tapis APPI -60.
A late September North West Shelf condensate was also confirmed bought by a European trader who was heard to have accumulated a large volume of NWS condensate to take to its refinery in Australia.
The direction of the heavy crude market was less clear, with premiums discussed at varying levels.
August Minas was rumoured sold by a shosha at ICP +15 cents, the lowest levels seen since July.
At least one shosha is still looking to sell August Minas, although the volume was small, around 100,000 barrels.
But an equity producer sold August Duri on Wednesday at ICP +80, was offering September Minas at ICP +60.
Minas was trading around 40 cents per barrel under Duri in July and early August.
The Middle East crude market remained lacklustre.
Rumours that a European major had sold a September Masila to a South Korean refiner at OSP -45 cents was denied by the refiner.
